description: The image consists of two vertically stacked bar charts illustrating the "% point difference" across different layers for two models, titled "mBERT" (top) and "XLM-R" (bottom). The horizontal axis represents the categories, labeled "layer" on the bottom chart, displaying discrete sequential categories ordered from 0 to 12, followed by a final category labeled "concat" on the bottom chart; the corresponding label position on the top chart is covered by a solid grey rectangle. The vertical axis on both charts represents the value, labeled "% point difference," using a linear scale that ranges from approximately -10.5 to slightly above 0. Numeric tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines are spaced at intervals of 2, specifically at -10, -8, -6, -4, -2, and 0. In the top "mBERT" chart, the bars are light blue with black outlines. These bars primarily extend downward from the zero line, with the most negative value at layer 0 (approximately -10.5) and a general trend of decreasing magnitude through layer 8. Layers 9, 10, and the final obscured category show small positive values (ranging from approximately +0.1 to +0.4), while layers 11 and 12 show negative values (approximately -0.2 and -1.2). In the bottom "XLM-R" chart, the bars are steel blue with black outlines. The bars start with the most negative values at layers 0 and 1 (both approximately -9.5) and progressively become less negative up to layer 9 (approximately -0.3). Layers 10, 11, and "concat" display small positive values (approximately +0.4), while layer 12 shows a slight negative value (approximately -0.2). The bars in both subplots are ordered sequentially by layer number followed by the final category, and all bars are visually defined by a thin black outline.
